newsitem.title: CANADA: Laidlaw sees US$3.6 bln in revs by 1998.
newsitem.headline: Laidlaw sees US$3.6 bln in revs by 1998.

text.p: Transportation and waste disposal giant Laidlaw Inc expects to see annualized revenues reach US$3.6 billion by end-April, 1998, President and Chief Executive Officer James Bullock told the annual meeting on Tuesday.

Once Laidlaw absorbs American Medical Response Inc of Colorado and completes a reverse take-over of Rollins Environmental Services Inc of Delaware, it will be close to a goal of hitting $4-$5 billion in yearly revenues by about 2000, Bullock said.
"I believe we're slightly ahead of schedule," Bullock said. Laidlaw announced the deals, totalling $2 billion, last week.
The revenues breakdown would be: $1.3 billion for its bus division, $1.3 billion for its ambulance and healthcare unit and $1.0 billion for waste disposal.
Bullock also said the giant will change its acquisition strategy in the ambulance and emergency arena for the fiscal year ended August 31.
"The nature of the acquisitions you'll see us making in this business going forward will be a lot of smaller acquisitions," (with) a few million (dollars) in revenue, Bullock said.

Laidlaw will be busy in fiscal 1997, integrating its operations after swallowing the bus unit of Scott's Hospitality Inc last year for C$836 million and making these "tuck-in" purchases, Bullock said.

Bullock said he expects Laidlaw will eventually cut back on its 66 percent stake in the new Rollins/Laidlaw firm called Laidlaw Environmental Services Inc. "I think it's safe to assume that over time, we will look to reduce our investment in Laidlaw/Rollins."
Laidlaw has pursued a strategy of divesting its waste business, most recently selling solid waste operations to Allied Waste Industries Inc for over $1.6 billion in September last year.
Laidlaw's Class B stock was up 0.40 to 17.85 on the Toronto Stock Exchange in afternoon trade, just below a year high of 18.00 set last week.
